# Interactive tool forms (MCP Apps)

A tool on an MCP server can show the user a form in the CUGA chat, wait for the user to fill it in,
and then return the result to the agent. For example, a tool can ask for contact details, show a
proposed table design for the user to edit, or collect an approval with comments.

CUGA supports the [MCP Apps](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/extensions/apps) standard, which
grew out of [MCP-UI](https://mcpui.dev). There is nothing to turn on in CUGA: a tool opens a form
when its MCP server declares one.

<Callout type="info">
Requires a CUGA version that includes MCP Apps support.
</Callout>

## How it works

1. The agent calls a tool whose metadata names a UI resource (`_meta.ui.resourceUri = "ui://..."`).
2. CUGA pauses the turn and shows the resource, an HTML page, in the chat.
3. The page calls tools on its own server through CUGA, for example to validate what the user entered.
4. When the user is done, the page tells CUGA what the agent should receive. The agent continues
   with that as the result of the tool call from step 1.

If the user closes the form instead, the agent is told the form was cancelled and asks how to continue.

## Who can call which tool

Each tool's `_meta.ui.visibility` says who may call it:

| Visibility | The agent can call it | The form can call it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `["model", "app"]` (default) | Yes | Yes |
| `["model"]` | Yes | No |
| `["app"]` | No, and it is not listed to the agent | Yes |

Use `["app"]` for the form's own actions, such as "save" or "validate", so the agent never calls them itself.

## Example: a contact details form

This MCP server, written with [FastMCP](https://gofastmcp.com) (tested with FastMCP 4.1), has two tools:

- `ask_contact_details` is called by the agent and opens the form.
- `save_contact_details` is called only by the form. It checks the email address and returns the saved details.

```python title="contact_form_server.py"
from fastmcp import FastMCP
from fastmcp.apps.config import AppConfig, ResourceCSP
from fastmcp.tools import ToolResult
from mcp.types import TextContent

mcp = FastMCP("contact_form")
FORM_URI = "ui://contact-form/form"

FORM_HTML = """<!doctype html>
<html>
  <body>
    <form id="form">
      <p id="reason"></p>
      <label>Name <input name="name" required></label>
      <label>Email <input name="email" type="email" required></label>
      <button>Submit</button>
      <p id="message"></p>
    </form>
    <script type="module">
      import { App } from "https://esm.sh/@modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps@1.7.5/app-with-deps";

      const app = new App({ name: "contact-form", version: "1.0.0" });
      // The result of ask_contact_details, the call that opened this form.
      app.ontoolresult = (result) => {
        document.getElementById("reason").textContent = result.structuredContent?.reason ?? "";
      };
      await app.connect();

      document.getElementById("form").onsubmit = async (event) => {
        event.preventDefault();
        const values = Object.fromEntries(new FormData(event.target));
        // Calls the app-only tool on this server, through CUGA.
        const saved = await app.callServerTool({ name: "save_contact_details", arguments: values });
        if (!saved.structuredContent?.ok) {
          document.getElementById("message").textContent = saved.content[0].text;
          return;
        }
        // What the agent receives as the result of ask_contact_details.
        await app.updateModelContext({ structuredContent: saved.structuredContent });
        // Finishes the form: CUGA resumes the agent.
        await app.sendMessage({ role: "user", content: [{ type: "text", text: "Contact details submitted." }] });
      };
    </script>
  </body>
</html>
"""


@mcp.tool(app=AppConfig(resource_uri=FORM_URI, visibility=["model", "app"]))
def ask_contact_details(reason: str) -> ToolResult:
    """Ask the user for their name and email address in a form."""
    return ToolResult(
        content=[TextContent(type="text", text=f"Asked the user for contact details: {reason}")],
        structured_content={"reason": reason},
    )


@mcp.tool(app=AppConfig(visibility=["app"]))
def save_contact_details(name: str, email: str) -> ToolResult:
    """Form action: check and save the details the user entered."""
    if "@" not in email:
        return ToolResult(
            content=[TextContent(type="text", text="Enter a valid email address.")],
            structured_content={"ok": False},
        )
    return ToolResult(
        content=[TextContent(type="text", text=f"Saved contact details for {name}.")],
        structured_content={"ok": True, "name": name, "email": email},
    )


@mcp.resource(FORM_URI, app=AppConfig(csp=ResourceCSP(resource_domains=["https://esm.sh"])))
def contact_form() -> str:
    return FORM_HTML


if __name__ == "__main__":
    mcp.run(transport="http", host="127.0.0.1", port=8220)
```

The form page loads the MCP Apps client library from `esm.sh`, so the resource declares that domain
in its CSP (`resource_domains`). Without a declaration the form has no network access at all; you
can also inline the library in the page instead.

Run the server, then point CUGA at it:

```bash
python contact_form_server.py
```

```yaml title="mcp_servers.yaml"
mcpServers:
  contact_form:
    url: http://127.0.0.1:8220/mcp
    transport: http
    description: Collect contact details from the user in a form.
```

```bash
MCP_SERVERS_FILE=$PWD/mcp_servers.yaml cuga start demo
```

Open `http://localhost:7860/chat` and ask, for example, *"Call ask_contact_details to ask me for my
contact details for the newsletter, then tell me what was saved."* The form appears in the chat.
After you submit it, the agent continues and answers with the saved name and email address.

## What the form sends back

The page uses the MCP Apps client library (`@modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps`):

| Call | What CUGA does |
| --- | --- |
| `app.ontoolresult` | Receives the result of the tool call that opened the form |
| `app.callServerTool(...)` | Calls a tool on the form's own server (visibility must include `"app"`) |
| `app.updateModelContext({ structuredContent })` | Stores what the agent receives as the tool's result |
| `app.sendMessage({ role: "user", content })` | Finishes the form; the text is passed to the agent as the user's message |

If the page sends no model context, the agent receives the result of the form's last tool call.

## Where forms appear

Forms appear only in the CUGA web chat. Everywhere else, including the Python SDK, API clients of
`/stream`, channels and other agents, a tool with a UI returns its ordinary result and the run does
not wait for a form. Design the tool's result so the agent can still act on it without the form.

## Security

- The form runs in a sandboxed iframe on a **different origin** from the chat, through a proxy page
  that CUGA serves at `/mcp-apps/sandbox_proxy.html`.
- The form's network access follows the resource's `_meta.ui.csp`. With no CSP declared, it has none.
- The browser only names the interaction. Which server, resource and tools a form may reach is
  decided by the CUGA server, and a form cannot call tools without `"app"` visibility.

## Deployment

Locally there is nothing to configure: CUGA serves the form from the other spelling of the same
host (`localhost` and `127.0.0.1`). Behind a real domain, give the form its own origin that reaches
the same CUGA server, and set:

| Environment variable | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `CUGA_MCP_APPS_SANDBOX_ORIGIN` | Origin that serves `/mcp-apps/sandbox_proxy.html` for forms, for example `https://cuga-sandbox.example.com`. It must differ from the chat's origin. Without it, forms do not open on hosts other than `localhost` and `127.0.0.1`. |
| `CUGA_MCP_APPS_HOST_ORIGINS` | Comma-separated chat origins allowed to embed that page, for example `https://cuga.example.com`. |

## Limitations

- Supported for MCP server tools in CugaLite, in both CodeAct and function-calling modes.
- A form that is still open when the CUGA server restarts cannot be continued. Start the task again.
